items.q: Which summary of the warm-up times is resistant to the outlier at 45 minutes?

why.correct: The median depends only on the middle of the ordered data.
options: Right: it depends only on the middle values.
The mean adds 45 in, so it moves.
The standard deviation uses every distance from the mean.

items.q: What is the median warm-up time, in minutes?

why.correct: The ordered 7th and 8th values are 15 and 16, so the median is 15.5.

mistakes.why: That is the mean, not the median: order the data and take the middle value.

items.q: What is the interquartile range of the warm-up times, in minutes?

why.correct: $Q_1 = 13$ and $Q_3 = 20$ (the medians of each half), so $\text{IQR} = 7$.

mistakes.why: That is the range, the maximum minus the minimum; the IQR is Q3 minus Q1.

items.q: By the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule, which warm-up times are outliers?

why.correct: The upper fence is $20 + 1.5(7) = 30.5$; only 45 is above it, and nothing is below $13 - 10.5 = 2.5$.
options: Right: 45 is the only value above 30.5.
9 is well above the lower fence of 2.5.
Right: the two values at least 2.

items.q: Using the table, what is the mean (expected value) of $X$?

options: Right: each value weighted by its probability.
That averages 0, 1, 2 and 3 without the probabilities.
That is the most likely value, not the mean.

items.q: Which statement about the table is true?

why.correct: A probability distribution's probabilities add to 1.
options: X takes only whole-number values, so it is discrete.

items.q: Placeholder: a 95% interval for a mean, from $\bar{x} = 18.36$, $s = 9.06$ and $n = 14$.
Write the expression for the z-score of a warm-up time of 30 minutes, using the mean 18.36 and standard deviation 9.06.

why.correct: A z-score is the value minus the mean, over the standard deviation.

mistakes.why: Subtract in the order value minus mean, so a value above the mean has a positive z-score.

items.q: What is the z-score of a warm-up time of 30 minutes, using mean 18.36 and standard deviation 9.06?

mistakes.why: The sign is backward: value minus mean, not mean minus value.

items.q: Placeholder: state the conclusion of a test with p-value 0.012 at $\alpha = 0.05$.

why.correct: Because 0.012 < 0.05, reject the null hypothesis: convincing evidence for the alternative.

why.2: A test gives evidence; it never proves.

options: the true mean warm-up time of all players

conclude.model: Because the p-value of 0.012 is less than 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis. There is convincing evidence that the true mean warm-up time of all players is greater than 15 minutes.
